studies.name: IPCC AR6 WGIII — Climate Change 2022: Mitigation of Climate Change (Chapter 12)
studies.draft_uses: Qualitative and structural claims about CDR roles, net-zero definitions, technology readiness, DACCS life-cycle emissions, and the framing that CDR is necessary but not a substitute for emissions cuts (robust evidence, high agreement)
studies.latest_known: AR6 WGIII (2022) remains the most recently published IPCC assessment report on mitigation. The IPCC AR7 WGIII first-order draft was circulated for expert review in November 2026 but has not been published. A 2027 IPCC Methodology Report on CDR Technologies and CCUS is in first-order expert review (2 Nov–20 Dec 2026).
studies.what_changed: No published successor to AR6 WGIII exists as of 2026-11-27. AR7 WGIII is in draft only; no figures have been formally superseded.

studies.name: Lamb et al. (2024) — 'The carbon dioxide removal gap', Nature Climate Change 14(6):644–651
studies.draft_uses: CDR gap framing; claim that current CDR 'approximates 2 GtCO2 per year, or about 3% of current global net greenhouse gas emissions'; national proposals fall short of 1.5°C scenarios; most ambitious proposals align with low-energy-demand scenario; no countries commit to novel methods at scale
studies.latest_known: The State of Carbon Dioxide Removal, 3rd Edition (June 2, 2026) by Edwards, Geden, Gidden, Lamb, Minx, Nemet, Smith et al. updates the current CDR figure to 2.2 GtCO2/year (~5% of gross CO2 emissions). The 2026 SoCDR also updates the CDR gap: 0.3 GtCO2 in 2030 and 5.2 GtCO2 in 2050 under highest-ambition scenarios. The Lamb et al. (2024) paper itself is the published version of the preprint; no retraction or correction has been issued, but its headline current-CDR figure has been updated by the 2026 SoCDR.
studies.what_changed: Current CDR moves from ~2 GtCO2/yr to 2.2 GtCO2/yr; the share of global emissions moves from ~3% of net GHG emissions to ~5% of gross CO2 emissions. The CDR gap in 2050 is now quantified at 5.2 GtCO2 (vs the 2024 paper's lower-bound gap of 3.2 GtCO2). The draft's '2 GtCO2' and '3%' figures are both stale.

studies.draft_uses: Claims about CDR not being a substitute for emissions reductions; 8:2 ratio of effort between reducing and removing CO2 by mid-century; CDR potentially allowing temperature exceedance reversal but not compensating for overshoot impacts; separate policy tracks for reductions and removals
studies.latest_known: The paper was published 17 September 2024 in Frontiers in Climate (doi: 10.3389/fclim.2024.1425971). No retraction, correction, or direct successor updating its specific figures has been identified. The paper is a systematic map of governance literature, not a quantitative scenario study, so its qualitative findings are less susceptible to numerical supersession.
studies.what_changed: No figures changed. The paper's qualitative governance findings remain the latest from this source.

studies.name: Fuss et al. (2018) — 'Negative emissions—Part 2: Costs, potentials and side effects', Environmental Research Letters 13:063002
studies.draft_uses: 2050 sustainable global potentials: afforestation/reforestation 0.5–3.6 GtCO2/yr, BECCS 0.5–5, biochar 0.5–2, enhanced weathering 2–4, DACCS 0.5–5, soil carbon up to 5; net zero CO2 reached globally between 2046 and 2056 in 1.5°C pathways; NETs deployment 5–15 GtCO2/yr by 2050 in most scenarios; soil carbon sinks saturate after 10–100 years; cooling from net-negative emissions may only offset part of earlier warming
studies.latest_known: The IPCC AR6 WGIII (2022) substantially updates these potential ranges: DACCS potential is now assessed at 5–40 GtCO2/yr (vs 0.5–5 in Fuss 2018), and the AR6 TS gives cumulative BECCS of 328 (168–763) GtCO2 and DACCS of 29 (0–339) GtCO2 across 2°C scenarios. The State of CDR 3rd Edition (June 2026) gives a central range of 7–9 GtCO2/yr total CDR needed by 2050 in Paris-compatible scenarios, with a highest-ambition median of 8.8 GtCO2/yr. The 2046–2056 net-zero CO2 timing range is from a 2018 scenario review and has been superseded by AR6 scenario analysis.
studies.what_changed: DACCS potential range in the draft (0.5–5 GtCO2/yr) is far below the AR6 WGIII assessment (5–40 GtCO2/yr). Total CDR needed by 2050 in the draft ('5–15 GtCO2/yr in most scenarios') is broadly consistent with newer estimates but the lower bound is now anchored at ~7 GtCO2/yr (central range) per SoCDR 3rd edition. The net-zero CO2 timing window (2046–2056) is a 2018 scenario-review figure not updated in the draft despite AR6 providing a more recent scenario synthesis. The 8:2 ratio of reductions to removals attributed to [4] (Lück et al.) may itself derive from Fuss 2018 framing.
